text:
mike: CI alert — infra/gpu-provision workflow is failing repeatedly this morning. Started at ~06:10. Symptoms: actions/cache restore returns 403, then gha runners retry and we hit our concurrency limit so terraform/helm steps queue and time out. Example from a run:
```
Run actions/cache@v3 restore
Error: Failed to download cache: Response status code does not indicate success: 403 (Forbidden).
...
helm upgrade --install gpu-nodepool ./charts/gpu --timeout 10m0s
Error: UPGRADE FAILED: context deadline exceeded
```
Anyone seen this pattern before? It's blocking a bunch of PRs for capacity fixes.

alesha: yep saw this earlier on a different job — cache 403 usually from transient token issue or the restore key being too large. But the bigger problem is GHA concurrency: when restore hangs our matrix spawns and then the concurrency group cancels older jobs which leaves partial state (helm started but never finished). :grimacing:

joel: also noticing many of these runs are landing on preemptible/self-hosted spot runners in us-west1-gpu and those VMs are getting reclaimed mid-helm. That makes the helm --timeout leak state. We should prefer non-preemptible for provisioning runs or add stronger leader election in the chart hooks.

tania: quick mitigation: 1) disable cache restore for the gpu-provision workflow (we don't get much benefit there), 2) increase helm timeout to 20m and add `--atomic` so failed upgrades roll back, 3) set a smaller concurrency window so we don't cancel in-progress apply jobs. I'll open a PR with changes.

mike: thanks Tania — can you also add a short check to the GH action to fail fast on 403 so we don't spin up extra matrix jobs? The current retry loop is what sucks up runner slots.

infra-bot: Deploy check: runner-pool-us-west1-gpu has 2 of 8 nodes NotReady (since 06:05). Autoscaler attempted scale up but quota error: compute.googleapis.com/quotaExceeded -> requesting increase.

joel: quotaExceeded explains why new dedicated runners weren't provisioned. Combined with spot preemptions it's a perfect storm. I'll ping cloud-ops to expedite quota request.

sam: oncall here — I'll temporarily mark the gpu runner pool as protected to avoid using preemptible instances for current workflow runs and add a label for provisioning jobs so they land on stable hosts. Doing that now.

alesha: after those changes, let's keep cache disabled for 24h and watch CI queue length. If we still see cache 403s on other infra jobs, open a separate infra-caching ticket (maybe the GHA token rotation bug).

mike: summary actions: Tania PR to disable cache + bump helm timeout + atomic, Sam to protect runner pool and add label, Joel to chase quota, Alesha to monitor cache errors. Thanks — this is blocking a handful of hotfix PRs so please ping in thread with progress. :thumbsup:

sam: update — runner label applied, one provisioning job re-ran and succeeded (no cache restore). Will follow up if quota reply comes back.
